## Problem

`pm-changelog --check` reports `Drift classification: tracker_changed` when the committed `CHANGELOG.md` has CRLF line endings and is otherwise identical to the generated output. This happens on a Windows runner whose Git checkout uses `core.autocrlf=true`.

The drift report then prints every line as changed (`@@ -1,536 +1,536 @@`), so the real cause is hard to see. The failure is also misclassified: the tracker didn't change; only the line endings differ.

## Evidence

pm-brief#228, required check `audit-windows` (job 133756411714):
- `test (22)` and `test (26)` passed the same `changelog:check` on Linux.
- The Windows job failed with `tracker_changed`.
- After stripping `\r`, all 536 committed lines match the generated lines, including all eleven `### Closed` blocks.

pm-brief now works around it with `.gitattributes` `CHANGELOG.md text eol=lf` (commit 2c7e8b4). Any fleet repository that runs `changelog:check` on Windows without that rule has the same latent failure.

## Expected

- `--check` compares content after normalizing CRLF to LF on both sides, or reports a separate `line_endings_only` drift classification with a clear remedy, such as adding `CHANGELOG.md text eol=lf`.
- The drift diff is computed on the normalized text, so it shows only real changes.
- A regression test covers a CRLF-only difference: it either passes, or fails with the dedicated classification. It never reports `tracker_changed`.
changelog --check reports tracker_changed for a CRLF-only difference on Windows checkouts
